verses.text: The whole community of Israel left the desert of Sin, travelling from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
So they argued with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." Moses answered, "Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing the LORD?"
But the people were thirsty for water there, and they grumbled against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt? Was it to kill us, our children, and our animals with thirst?"
Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with these people? They are almost ready to throw stones at me."
The LORD answered Moses, "Walk on ahead of the people. Take some of the leaders of Israel with you, and take in your hand the staff you used to strike the Nile, and go.
I will stand there in front of you by the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it for the people to drink." So Moses did this while the leaders of Israel watched.
He called the place Massah, which means testing, and Meribah, which means arguing, because the people of Israel argued, and because they tested the LORD by saying, "Is the LORD with us or not?"
Then the Amalekites came and attacked the people of Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some men for us and go out to fight the Amalekites. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
So Joshua did what Moses told him and fought the Amalekites, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
As long as Moses held up his hands, the Israelites were winning. But whenever he lowered his hands, the Amalekites were winning.
When Moses' arms grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on each side. So his hands stayed steady until sunset.
So Joshua defeated the Amalekite army with the sword.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this in a book so that it will be remembered, and make sure Joshua hears it. I will completely wipe out the memory of the Amalekites from under heaven."
Moses built an altar and called it "The LORD is my Banner."
He said, "The LORD has made a promise: the LORD will be at war with the Amalekites in every generation."
